town.name: Mueang Chiang Mai (the old walled city)

households.livelihood: rice, corn, tobacco and cabbage farming with livestock
handicrafts: silverware, embroidery, silk, celadon, lacquerware, woodcarving, parasols
tourism and trade; the province is the tourist hub of the north

landmarks.name: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep
landmarks.note: Gold chedi about 24 m tall on an octagonal base with a tiered umbrella top, reached by 309 steps lined with naga balustrades.

landmarks.name: Wat Chedi Luang
landmarks.note: Founded 1401; a large old brick chedi in the walled city, damaged by an earthquake in the 16th century.

landmarks.name: Doi Inthanon
landmarks.note: Forested mountain, 2,565 m, the highest in Thailand.

households.livelihood: rice, corn, tobacco and cabbage farming

households.home: farm home on the northern slopes
households.livelihood: coffee, pineapple, coconut and banana growing

landmarks.name: Wat Rong Khun
landmarks.note: All-white contemporary Lanna-style temple with a three-tiered roof, many nagas and mirror-glass chips that sparkle.

landmarks.name: Doi Tung
landmarks.note: Mountain of 1,389 m in the north of the province, the province's key terrain feature.

landmarks.name: Kok River
landmarks.note: The river that flows through Chiang Rai city.

households.livelihood: ceramics: over 200 factories in and around Mueang Lampang
lignite mining and the coal-fired power plant

households.home: farm home in the Wang valley

landmarks.name: Wat Phra That Lampang Luang
landmarks.note: Teak Lanna temple with a bronze-sheathed bell-shaped chedi and an open-sided vihara with three-tiered shingle roof and tall wooden columns.

landmarks.name: Wat Sri Chum
landmarks.note: Burmese-style temple in Lampang.

households.home: orchard house in the Ping valley
households.livelihood: longan orchards; a longan festival is held each August

households.home: farm house at the edge of town

landmarks.name: Wat Phra That Hariphunchai
landmarks.note: Bell-shaped central chedi with repousse Buddha images on bronze sheets; on the one-satang coin.

landmarks.name: Chedi Suwanna
landmarks.note: Pyramid-shaped Dvaravati-style stupa about 46 m tall (Wikipedia places it in the same compound).

landmarks.name: Ko Luang Waterfall
landmarks.note: Waterfall in Mae Ping National Park.

nameTh: แม่ฮ่องสอน

households.home: mountain-village home; it was the poorest province in 2012
households.livelihood: farming in a province that is 85.5% forest

households.home: town house near the main market
households.livelihood: guesthouses and trips to hill villages, caves and waterfalls

landmarks.name: Wat Phrathat Doi Kong Mu
landmarks.note: Temple on Doi Kong Mu, a hill above the town.

landmarks.name: Mae Surin Falls
landmarks.note: Described as the highest waterfall in northern Thailand.

landmarks.name: Pang Oung
landmarks.note: Reservoir in Mueang Mae Hong Son district.

households.home: farm house in the Nan valley
households.livelihood: farming and fishing: 53% of the workforce, 29% of output (2022)
administrative, educational and hospital work in town

landmarks.name: Wat Phumin
landmarks.note: Cross-shaped ordination hall (1596) that seems to rest on two giant nagas, with four entrances and teak pillars.

landmarks.name: Wat Phra That Chang Kham
landmarks.note: Chedi with gilded elephant heads.

landmarks.name: Wat Phra That Khao Noi
landmarks.note: Fifteenth-century temple on a hill over the city with a golden standing Buddha.

households.livelihood: crops and livestock on farmland watered by Kwan Phayao (16,500 families nearby)

landmarks.name: Kwan Phayao
landmarks.note: Shallow lake of 19.8 km2 beside the town, the largest freshwater lake in the north.

landmarks.name: Wat Si Khom Kham
landmarks.note: Temple housing Phra Chao Ton Luang, a seated Buddha about 18 m high.

landmarks.name: Doi Luang
landmarks.note: Mountain of 1,694 m that rises over the Phayao valley.

households.livelihood: textile industry (the town is known for textiles; no detail given)

landmarks.name: Phra That Cho Hae
landmarks.note: Stupa on a hill about 9 km southeast of the town; the provincial symbol.

landmarks.name: Phae Mueang Phi
landmarks.note: Eroded mushroom rocks and pillars of earth a few km north of town.

households.livelihood: durian and langsat orchards (about 20,000 t of durian in 2012)

landmarks.name: Wat Phra Thaen Sila At
landmarks.note: Temple whose mondop sits on a laterite block; shown on the provincial seal.

landmarks.name: Ton Sak Yai teak tree
landmarks.note: Teak tree over 1,500 years old with a trunk about 9.87 m round, in Ton Sak Yai National Park (kind is a stand-in; no tree kind exists).

landmarks.name: Nan River
landmarks.note: The river whose valley the province lies in.
